Failure to Investigate and Inaccurate Reporting : Under the FCRA, when a consumer disputes information with a credit reporting agency, the agency must notify the furnisher, who is then required to investigate and correct or delete any inaccurate information. 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( b ). To state a claim under this provision, a plaintiff must allege that a dispute was filed with a consumer reporting agency, that the agency notified the furnisher, and that the furnisher failed to investigate and correct the inaccurate information. Courts have held that " a showing of inaccuracy is essential '' for an FCRA claim against a furnisher. Contradictory Reporting : The reporting of the account as both " charged-off '' and with a " past due balance '' is materially contradictory and misleading. A " charge-off '' indicates that the creditor has written the debt off as a loss and closed the account. Reporting a " past due '' balance after a charge-off creates a confusing and inaccurate picture of the account 's status, which can unfairly damage a consumer 's creditworthiness. Courts have recognized this as a potential basis for an FCRA claim. Failure to XXXX a Reasonable Investigation : My direct requests to XXXX XXXX for validation, coupled with the dispute of this account, triggered a duty to conduct a reasonable investigation. XXXX XXXX 's failure to respond to my request for documentation constitutes a failure to conduct a reasonable reinvestigation as required by law. This is not a mere technicality ; it is a substantive violation that prevents me from verifying the debt 's validity. Inaccuracy as a Matter of Law : In XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, a court recently held that if subsequent repayment plans or assignments do not legally modify the original loan terms, the reporting of the original status as a " charge-off '' may remain accurate. However, this logic cuts the other way for you : if the debt has been sold or assigned to a third party, or if the details of the account ( like the balance ) can not be verified, then XXXX XXXX 's continued reporting of the original status and balance becomes inaccurate and violates the FCRA. The central question is whether XXXX XXXX can prove the information it is reporting is accurate. 2. Violations of the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ), 15 U.S.C. 1692 et seq. Radius Global Solutions LLC, as a third-party debt collector, is subject to the FDCPA. XXXX XXXX, as the original creditor, is generally exempt from the FDCPA. However, the third-party agencies it hires are not. Failure to Validate Debt : Under 15 U.S.C. 1692g, a debt collector must cease collection activities until it provides verification of the debt to the consumer if a timely validation request is made. My receipt of a collection notice from a different agency prior to Radius, and my subsequent request for validation, triggers this duty. I have not received adequate validation from either agency, which is a direct violation of the FDCPA. Misrepresentation and Deceptive Practices : The use of multiple collection agencies to collect the same debt constitutes a deceptive practice under the FDCPA. It suggests that the debt may have been " sold '' or " assigned '' to multiple parties, creating confusion about who has the legal right to collect, or that the debt amount is being " double-dipped '' or inflated. See 15 U.S.C. 1692e ( prohibiting false, deceptive, or misleading representations in connection with debt collection ). 3. Violations of the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act ( GLBA ), 15 U.S.C. 6801 et seq. XXXX XXXX 's transfer of my nonpublic personal financial information ( NPI ) to third-party collection agencies raises serious privacy concerns. Under the GLBA, financial institutions are required to protect the privacy of consumer information and provide consumers with a privacy notice explaining their information-sharing practices. If XXXX XXXX transferred my information to multiple collection agencies without a permissible legal basis or proper notice, it may constitute a violation of federal privacy law. I request that XXXX XXXX explain the legal basis for these disclosures. XXXX. The " Nonsensical '' Nature of this Debt The circumstances of this debt do not make logical sense and should be a red flag for the CFPB : Assignment vs. Ownership : The debt is being reported by XXXX XXXX as a charge-off. This often indicates the debt has been sold to a third party. If it was sold, XXXX XXXX no longer has a financial interest in it and should stop reporting a balance. If it was not sold, XXXX XXXX owns the debt and should be able to provide documentation. The fact that multiple collection agencies are involved suggests ownership is unclear. The Chain of Title is Broken : A debt is a financial asset. When it is sold or assigned, there must be a clear " chain of title '' a paper trail showing each transfer of ownership. The involvement of multiple collection agencies suggests this chain is broken. XXXX XXXX and Radius must produce all documents proving a clear chain of title. The Request for Validation Was Ignored : If XXXX XXXX and Radius can not produce a contract with my signature, an accounting of the balance, and proof of their authority to collect, then this alleged debt is unverifiable and can not be reported. An explanation of why XXXX XXXX continues reporting this account if it can not provide documentation supporting the accuracy and legal basis of the reporting. An investigation into XXXX XXXX 's credit reporting practices, specifically regarding the contradictory reporting of charged-off accounts with outstanding balances. An order for all violations to cease. If the requested documentation can not be produced, I request that the CFPB order XXXX XXXX and its agents to : Delete the tradeline from all consumer credit reports. Cease all collection efforts regarding this alleged debt. Conclusion The law is clear : consumers have the right to verify the debts that are being reported against them. Consumer complaint narrative: * * What Happened * * I am submitting this complaint because * * Diversified Adjustment Service, Inc. * * continues to report a collection account on my consumer credit reports that I believe is inaccurate, incomplete, misleading, and has not been properly verified as required by the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ). I exercised my rights under the FCRA by disputing this account with the consumer reporting agencies and requesting that a reasonable reinvestigation be conducted. Despite my dispute, Diversified Adjustment Service continues to report the account without providing competent documentary evidence establishing that the information is accurate or that it has the legal authority to collect and report the alleged debt. Instead of providing the documentation I requested, I have received only generalized responses indicating that the account was " verified '' or that it will continue to be reported. These responses do not explain what records were reviewed, what evidence was relied upon, or how Diversified Adjustment Service concluded that every aspect of the reporting was accurate. A statement that an account has been verified, without providing supporting documentation, does not satisfy the requirements of the Fair Credit Reporting Act. The Diversified Adjustment Service collection account continues to appear as a derogatory collection account on my consumer credit reports and has caused substantial harm to my financial standing. Collection accounts have a significant negative impact on a consumer 's credit profile because they are considered serious derogatory information by lenders, landlords, insurers, and employers. The continued reporting of this account affects my ability to obtain credit, qualify for favorable interest rates, secure housing, and pursue other financial opportunities. Because of these serious consequences, I requested that Diversified Adjustment Service conduct a complete investigation supported by original business records rather than relying solely upon automated verification systems or electronic responses. Under * * 15 U.S.C. 1681i * *, once a consumer disputes the accuracy of information appearing on a credit report, the consumer reporting agency must conduct a reasonable reinvestigation to determine whether the disputed information is accurate. Likewise, * * 15 U.S.C. 1681e ( b ) * * requires consumer reporting agencies to maintain reasonable procedures to assure the maximum possible accuracy of the information they report. These statutory obligations require more than forwarding a dispute electronically and accepting a computerized response from the furnisher. A reasonable investigation requires review of competent documentary evidence establishing that the disputed information is accurate, complete, and legally reportable. Because Diversified Adjustment Service is a third-party debt collector, I requested documentation establishing that it has the legal authority to collect and report the alleged debt. Specifically, I requested copies of any assignment agreements, transfer documents, servicing agreements, collection placement records, or any other documentation demonstrating that the alleged obligation was lawfully assigned or transferred to Diversified Adjustment Service. I also requested documentation identifying the original creditor, records establishing the complete chain of assignment, and documentation demonstrating that Diversified Adjustment Service has the legal authority to furnish information regarding this alleged account to the nationwide consumer reporting agencies. To date, I have not received competent documentary evidence establishing its legal authority to collect or report the alleged debt. In addition, I requested copies of the original agreement or contract that created the alleged obligation, documents bearing my signature, complete account statements, payment history, account ledger, documentation supporting the balance being reported, records establishing the date of first delinquency, documentation supporting any interest, collection fees, penalties, or additional charges added to the account, and every record relied upon during Diversified Adjustment Service 's investigation. If Diversified Adjustment Service contends that the account is accurate, then it should have no difficulty producing the original business records supporting every aspect of its reporting. Without these records, I have no reasonable basis to conclude that the information appearing on my consumer credit reports is accurate or legally reportable. I specifically requested disclosure of the method of verification used during the investigation. I requested the identity of the individual or department that conducted the investigation, the documents reviewed, the source of the information relied upon, and the procedures used to determine that the account was accurately reported. Instead of providing this information, Diversified Adjustment Service merely concluded that the account had been verified. This type of response provides no meaningful explanation regarding how the investigation was conducted and prevents me from determining whether Diversified Adjustment Service complied with its obligations under the Fair Credit Reporting Act. I am also concerned that the investigation conducted by the consumer reporting agencies relied primarily upon automated verification systems rather than an independent review of original source documentation. A reasonable investigation requires more than accepting a furnisher 's electronic confirmation without examining the underlying records. When a consumer specifically disputes a collection account and requests supporting evidence, the furnisher should review the original account records, assignment documents, collection placement records, payment history, account statements, and every other relevant business record before concluding that the account is accurate. Additionally, I dispute the balance currently being reported by Diversified Adjustment Service. If the reported balance includes accrued interest, collection fees, penalties, administrative charges, or other amounts, I request documentation explaining how those amounts were calculated, when they were added, and the contractual or statutory authority permitting those charges. If Diversified Adjustment Service can not fully substantiate the reported balance using contemporaneous business records, then the reported balance should be corrected or the account should be removed entirely. I also requested documentation establishing the date of first delinquency and demonstrating that the account is being reported within the period permitted under the Fair Credit Reporting Act. Consumer complaint narrative: DEMANDING CFPB INTERFERENCE IN THIS ONGOING ISSUE!! I NEED HELP! Re : Rebuttal to CFPB Complaint Nos. XXXX and XXXX This filing is my third CFPB complaint regarding this matter and serves as my formal rebuttal to both of my previous CFPB complaints, as well as the responses submitted by ProCollect. ProCollect is attempting to collect an alleged debt in the amount of {$3000.00} on behalf of XXXX at XXXX XXXX. From the outset of this dispute, I have consistently exercised my right to request validation of this alleged debt because I do not believe the debt has been substantiated. In both of my previous CFPB complaints, I specifically requested documentation sufficient to establish that this debt is legitimate and legally owed by me. My requests included, but were not limited to : A complete copy of the lease agreement bearing my signature. Any lease renewals, amendments, or extensions. An itemized move-out statement identifying every charge being claimed. A complete payment ledger showing all charges, credits, and payments. Documentation supporting any claim for unpaid rent. Documentation supporting the alleged early termination fee, including the lease provision authorizing such a charge and proof that the lease was actually terminated early. Move-out inspection reports. Repair invoices, photographs, or any documentation supporting alleged damages. Any documentation showing exactly how the balance of {$3000.00} was calculated. Despite making these requests in two separate CFPB complaints, ProCollect has failed to provide any of the documentation necessary to validate this alleged debt. Instead, ProCollect merely mailed what appears to be a self-generated, one-page invoice containing generalized descriptions such as " rent, '' " late charges, '' and " early termination fee. '' This document is not validation of a debt. It contains no signed lease, no lease renewals or extensions, no payment history, no accounting ledger, no move-out inspection report, no invoices, no repair documentation, no photographs, no proof of damages, no proof of unpaid rent, no documentation establishing that an early termination actually occurred, no documentation showing when the lease was scheduled to expire, and no evidence demonstrating how the balance being claimed was calculated. Most concerning, the document itself appears to contain a designated signature line for management approval that is completely unsigned. An unsigned, internally generated invoice created by either the creditor or its collection agency is not independent evidence that a debt exists, that the amount claimed is accurate, or that it is legally enforceable. It is merely an unsupported assertion by the party attempting to collect the debt. Even more troubling is ProCollect 's handling of my CFPB complaints. After carefully reviewing the responses submitted to both of my previous complaints, it is apparent that ProCollect simply copied and pasted its original response into the second complaint. The responses are virtually identical. The only substantive difference is that, in response to my first complaint, ProCollect stated that it " will mail proof of the debt to the consumer today on XXXX. '' In response to my second complaint, they merely changed that sentence to state that they " sent the proof on XXXX. '' Everything else remained substantially the same. This demonstrates that ProCollect did not conduct a new investigation, did not review the specific issues raised in my second complaint, and did not respond to my renewed request for actual debt validation. Instead, they recycled the same boilerplate response while completely ignoring the substance of my dispute. More importantly, what ProCollect claims to have mailed on XX/XX/XXXX still does not constitute validation. Mailing the same unsupported internal invoice does not satisfy my repeated requests for the underlying documentation establishing that I legally owe this debt. My second complaint clearly explained why the document previously provided was inadequate and specifically identified the documentation that remained missing. Rather than addressing any of those deficiencies, ProCollect simply submitted the same canned response and ignored every issue I raised. This pattern demonstrates an unwillingness to meaningfully investigate my dispute or provide competent evidence supporting the debt they continue to report. I am not required to pay {$3000.00} simply because a collection agency claims I owe it. If ProCollect is asserting that I have a legal obligation to pay this debt, then they should be able to produce the documents proving it. To date, they have failed to do so despite being given multiple opportunities through the CFPB complaint process. Their continued refusal to provide the requested documentation while simultaneously reporting this account to the nationwide consumer reporting agencies is causing substantial and ongoing financial harm. I am currently attempting to purchase a home, and this unverified collection account has already caused me to lose a home-buying opportunity. It continues to negatively impact my creditworthiness and my ability to qualify for mortgage financing. Consumers should not be forced to repeatedly dispute the same account while a collection agency responds with recycled, boilerplate language instead of conducting a meaningful investigation and producing competent documentary evidence. At this point, this matter has been before the CFPB on three separate occasions, and ProCollect still has not produced the basic documentation necessary to establish that this alleged debt is valid, accurate, or legally enforceable. The burden is on ProCollect to substantiate the debt they are attempting to collectnot on me to simply accept their unsupported assertions. Accordingly, I respectfully request that the CFPB require ProCollect to do one of two things : Produce complete documentary evidence validating this alleged debt, including the signed lease agreement, any renewals or extensions, a complete payment ledger, move-out documentation, documentation supporting every charge claimed, and all other records necessary to establish both liability and the accuracy of the amount being reported ; or Immediately cease all collection activity and request the permanent deletion of this collection account from XXXX XXXX, and XXXX because XXXX despite XXXX CFPB filings and repeated opportunities to substantiate the debt, ProCollect has failed to provide competent evidence that this alleged obligation is valid. I have acted in good faith throughout this process. I have repeatedly requested documentation that any reasonable consumer would expect before paying thousands of dollars to a collection agency. Rather than providing that documentation, ProCollect has repeatedly relied on an unsigned, self-generated internal invoice and recycled responses that fail to address my legitimate requests. After XXXX CFPB complaints, ProCollect has demonstrated either an inability or an unwillingness to validate this alleged debt. Their continued reporting of an unsubstantiated collection account is causing ongoing financial harm and undermines the accuracy and integrity of my credit file. For these reasons, I respectfully request that the CFPB require the immediate deletion of this collection account from XXXX, XXXX, and XXXX and grant the relief requested in my prior complaints.

Consumer complaint narrative: CRITICAL NOTICE TO INVESTIGATOR AND RESPONDENT : The CFPB electronic portal forces consumers to select from a restrictive list of predefined, automated dropdown categories to submit a form. The consumer has selected the closest available structural option ( " Dispute the Amount '' ) under protest solely to bypass portal formatting constraints.This submission is made strictly as a dispute regarding structural non-compliance, lack of statutory chain of title, and material misrepresentations by the collector. This filing does not constitute a validation of liability, an admission or acknowledgment of any alleged debt instrument, or a waiver of any consumer rights under federal or state law. The consumer reserves all rights to contest the existence, ownership, validity, and enforceability of the alleged balance in its entirety. I am submitting this formal complaint against Second Alliance , Inc. ( XXXX XXXX, CA ) for explicit violations of the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ), the Oregon Unlawful Debt Collection Practices Act ( OUDCPA ), and the California Rosenthal Act. The agency is engaging in unlawful continued collection activities and utilizing material misrepresentations to pressure me into an unsafe refinancing agreement. 1. Failure to Provide Mandatory Chain of Title Following an initial communication, Second Alliance , Inc. sent a validation packet containing only an underlying student loan contract executed with XXXX Bank. On XXXX XXXX XXXX, I exercised my rights under ORS 646A.670 and sent a formal statutory dispute noticing the deficiency. I demanded physical business recordssuch as an assignment agreement or bill of saleproving a clear, unbroken chain of ownership from the original creditor ( XXXX Bank ) to the current alleged owner. Second Alliance , Inc. failed to produce any physical transfer documentation. 2. False, Deceptive, and Contradictory Ownership Narrative Instead of pausing collection efforts to compile the statutory evidence, XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX sent a response letter containing a blatant factual and legal impossibility. The letter explicitly states : " The owner and loan holder is and has always been XXXX student loan. XXXX was the originating lender. '' Under 15 U.S.C. 1692e and Cal. Civ. Code 1788.17, debt collectors are strictly prohibited from using false or misleading representations regarding the character or legal status of a debt. An originating lender is, by definition, the first legal owner and holder of a signed promissory note. Therefore, Edly could not have " always '' been the holder. Furthermore, independent credit reporting data directly refutes the agency 's claim. The consumer 's credit profile shows the loan was held under " XXXX '' ( XXXX Bank ) until XX/XX/scrub>XXXX XXXX, moved to " XXXX '' for one month, and was explicitly marked " Transferred to another lender '' in XX/XX/scrub>XXXX XXXX This independent credit data proves that the loan has undergone multiple structural assignments and transfers, making the agency 's written claim of continuous, unbroken ownership a patently false misrepresentation designed to obscure a missing chain of title. 3. Unlawful Continued Collections and Refinancing Solicitation While my statutory validation request remained pending and unfulfilled, Second Alliance , Inc. actively continued collection efforts by attempting to solicit a {$350.00} voluntary payment to " re-age '' the loan. Furthermore, they used this deceptive ownership narrative to push a high-pressure solicitation to " refinance '' the debt through a partner lender. Under Oregon law ( ORS 646.639 ) and California 's Rosenthal Act ( Cal. Civ. Code 1788.17 ), a debt collector must completely cease and freeze all collection efforts upon receiving a consumer dispute until accurate validation is provided. Attempting to maneuver a consumer out of a highly disputable contract with missing ownership records and into a brand-new, refinanced loan agreement before validating the debt constitutes an unfair, deceptive, and abusive collection practice.

Consumer complaint narrative: Date : XXXX XXXX XXXX Re : Formal Notice of Dispute, Demand for Validation, and Immediate Deletion To Whom It May Concern, I am writing to formally dispute your alleged claim that I owe the above-referenced account. I dispute this debt in its entirety. This letter serves as my formal request for complete validation pursuant to the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ), 15 U.S.C. 1692 et seq., and my notice that any inaccurate reporting to any consumer reporting agency violates the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), 15 U.S.C. 1681 et seq. The original creditor has already admitted in writing that the alleged account was sold to another entity in XXXX and that it is no longer the creditor. If your company claims ownership today, then you bear the full burden of proving that you possess the legal right to collect this alleged obligation. Ownership of an alleged debt can not be presumed through account statements or computer-generated records. Statements merely reflect alleged activity ; they do not establish legal ownership, assignment, standing, or my contractual obligation to your company. Accordingly, provide competent admissible evidence establishing your legal authority to collect, including : The complete chain of title from the original creditor through every purchaser, assignee, and debt buyer to your company. Every purchase and sale agreement applicable to this specific account. Bills of Sale identifying my specific account by name and account number. Assignment agreements executed by authorized representatives. Proof that value was exchanged for this account. The complete original signed credit agreement bearing my signature. Proof that the alleged debt has not been previously settled, discharged, canceled, forgiven, or otherwise extinguished. Documentation establishing that the balance you claim is accurate, including a complete accounting of all fees, interest, payments, credits, and adjustments. Documentation demonstrating that you possess legal standing to enforce this alleged obligation in court. Documentation proving your authority to report this account to consumer reporting agencies. Please be advised that under the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act, you must cease collection activity until proper validation has been provided. Furthermore, under the Fair Credit Reporting Act : 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( b ) requires furnishers to conduct a reasonable investigation before verifying disputed information. 15 U.S.C. 1681e ( b ) requires maximum possible accuracy. 15 U.S.C. 1681i requires reinvestigation of disputed information. Reporting information that can not be verified constitutes inaccurate reporting. Verifying information without competent evidence is neither reasonable nor lawful. If your company has reported this account to Equifax, Experian, or TransUnion without possessing competent evidence establishing ownership and collectability, such reporting is inaccurate and misleading. Additionally, if this alleged debt has been sold multiple times, you must establish an uninterrupted chain of assignments from the original creditor to every subsequent purchaser. Failure to produce a complete chain of title means you can not establish standing or ownership. Please consider this letter notice that any continued reporting, collection activity, or verification without competent documentary evidence may constitute violations of : Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( 15 U.S.C. 1692e, 1692f, and 1692g ) Fair Credit Reporting Act ( 15 U.S.C. 1681e ( b ), 1681i, and 1681s-2 ( b ) ) Should your company continue reporting or collecting this disputed account without first producing competent legal evidence establishing ownership and standing, I reserve all rights to pursue every remedy available under federal and applicable state law, including filing complaints with the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau XXXX Federal Trade Commission , my State Attorney General, and seeking statutory damages, actual damages, attorney 's fees, and all other relief available by law. Nothing in this correspondence constitutes an acknowledgment of liability, an admission that any debt exists, or a promise to pay. I expressly reserve all rights.
